Interior design brief: modern eclectic, new furniture throughout

Fletcher House Refurnish

The same four-bedroom chalet bungalow, planned on the assumption that the current owners take every piece of furniture with them. Prepared for Neil Fletcher.

4 bedrooms, garage, garden room

The Brief

This is the empty-house version of the same scheme: everything freestanding, the sofas, beds, rugs, tables, chairs and wardrobes-that-aren't-fitted, leaves with the current owners, so it all gets bought new rather than kept and restyled. Two rooms also change job entirely: the attic room becomes archery storage and a fletching bench rather than a spare bedroom, and the garden room outbuilding becomes a woodwork workshop rather than a second lounge. No rattan or cane anywhere in the buy list, this time round. What doesn't move is whatever is actually part of the building:

  • The fitted kitchen, worktops and integrated oven and hob
  • The bathroom suite and tiling
  • The mirrored sliding wardrobes in bedrooms one and two
  • The bedroom one wallpaper and the fitted shutters throughout
  • Oak floors, doors, staircase and the built-in hall bookshelves
  • The garden room and outbuilding structures themselves

The same palette and material system carries over from the original brief, Plaster Putty as the unifying neutral, bottle green, terracotta and mustard as the accent trio, so the two versions would still look like one house if you mixed and matched. The difference is scale, plus a proper utility and home-gym fit-out that the first pass missed, and a genuinely darker, den-like treatment for the study rather than another guest room done in the house colours.

Palette & Materials
Plaster Putty#DED4C3

Unifying wall colour, matt emulsion, every room

Chalk Trim#F3EEE4

Skirting, architrave and ceilings throughout

Botanical Ink#33503F

Bottle green: living room, garden room, bedroom two

Terracotta Clay#B4552F

Burnt rust: bedroom two, garden room, outdoor cushions

Mustard Gold#C99A3E

Aged brass and ochre textiles: hallway, bedroom one

Midnight Denim#2B3A4A

Ink blue: bedroom one, living room accents

Blackened Steel#2A2A28

Hardware, tap ware, window frames

Peat Charcoal#26211C

Deep, cocooning wall colour: the study/den

Materials carried through every room

  • White oak: existing floors and doors, worked around, not fought
  • Reclaimed and solid oak: coffee tables, dining tables, freestanding storage
  • Boucle and linen: new sofas, upholstery and cushions
  • Jute and sisal: new rugs, entrance matting
  • Solid oak and ash: new bed frames, tables and freestanding storage
  • Brass and blackened steel: mixed metals, hardware and lighting
  • Rubber and steel: the workshop, archery room and home gym

How the trio is used

  • One accent per room, drawn from the trio: never more than two in the same space
  • Putty and chalk stay constant everywhere, as the thing that makes new furniture from different shops read as one scheme
  • Brass and blackened steel are mixed deliberately, not matched, across all hardware and lighting
The Plan

Ground floor runs living room and garden room off the same central spine, both opening toward the garden, worth treating as one continuous indoor-outdoor sequence rather than two separate schemes. Bedroom three, off the hall, is now a study rather than a guest room; the utility space next to the kitchen becomes utility-plus-gym. The attic room, the one space reached by its own stair, is now dedicated archery storage and a fletching bench rather than a bedroom, and the freestanding garden room outbuilding is a woodwork workshop rather than a second lounge.
